subject.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — a setState bridge capability + persisted widget state

question: Should OpenClaw accept dashboard widget write-back now, and should the persistent state contract be SQLite/plugin-state rather than per-widget JSON sidecars?
rationale: This adds a new stateful bridge for untrusted browser widgets plus persistent product state, so code inspection cannot settle the product, storage, and security boundary choices without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a SQLite-backed bridge
options.body: Keep the issue open and require any implementation to use plugin-state SQLite or an approved schema with explicit capability, approval, size, isolation, and security tests.

options.title: Narrow to API design first
options.body: Hold implementation PRs until maintainers first define the minimal plugin/dashboard API and storage contract for stateful widgets.

options.title: Defer until Wave 1 lands
options.body: Leave this as roadmap work and revisit only after the existing dashboard workspace and sandbox PRs are merged or rejected.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a SQLite-backed bridge
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require any implementation to use plugin-state SQLite or an approved schema with explicit capability, approval, size, isolation, and security tests.
